text:
sasha: Heads-up: I'm proposing a change to admission control for fleet saturation. TL;DR: staged soft-shedding by traffic class — short bounded queues for high-priority, graceful reject for best-effort. Details below.

jorge: How does this differ from the current `reject-first` policy? We saw a ~30% spike in tail latency last week.

sasha: Current: immediate 429 when queue full. Proposal summary: three tiers (P0/P1/P2). P0 = real-time: bounded queue (50ms) then degrade to quantized model or CPU fallback; P1 = standard: queue up to 200ms then 429; P2 = best-effort: immediate 429 with Retry-After. Also emit `X-Redwood-Admission` headers and structured JSON errors.

anika: How do we map traffic to tiers? route-level config or per-API-key mapping?

sasha: Per-route default + API-key overrides. Default mapping: streaming/chat endpoints -> P0/P1, bulk embeddings -> P2. Customers can opt into longer queue windows per key.

lee: Cost note: longer queues hold GPU contexts and can reduce effective throughput. Need `max_queued_per_gpu` and a short eviction window. Otherwise we trade latency for throughput loss.

sasha: Agreed. Plan includes `max_queued_per_gpu` and `eviction_ms` to prevent head-of-line blocking. Also a fallback chain: try quantized model, then CPU fallback for tiny requests.

jorge: Can you paste a prototype admission-controller config?

sasha: ```yaml
admission_controller:
  tiers:
    P0:
      queue_ms: 50
      max_queued_per_gpu: 8
      eviction_ms: 120
      fallback_chain: [quantized-v1, cpu-tiny]
    P1:
      queue_ms: 200
      max_queued_per_gpu: 16
      eviction_ms: 300
      fallback_chain: [quantized-v1]
    P2:
      queue_ms: 0
      max_queued_per_gpu: 4
      eviction_ms: 0
      fallback_chain: []
  emit_headers: true
  error_shape:
    code: "admission_rejected"
    fields: ["retry_after_ms","suggested_fallback"]
```

infra-bot: metric-alert: region us-east-1 GPU saturation > 92% (6m). Linked: /ops/fleet-dashboard :warning: 

anika: For multi-region behavior: prefer local soft-shedding first, then failover to remote region when the client latency budget allows. We need a routing policy that knows per-route SLOs.

lee: Backpressure propagation to SDKs is critical. Return `Retry-After` and `suggested_fallback` in the JSON so SDKs can either retry with backoff or switch to a cheaper model automatically.

sasha: Yep — standard error payload + `X-Redwood-Admission: P1;queued=120` header. Counters we will emit: admitted, queued, evicted, fallback_used, rejected.

jorge: SGTM. Suggest canary 5% traffic in us-east and eu-west to measure actual GPU hold time and fallbacks used.

sasha: Action items: (1) spike admission controller + metrics (jorge, sasha) (2) SDK error shape + header changes (anika) (3) canary config + runbook (lee). I'll open a PR with the YAML prototype and a short runbook today :rocket:
